activity.notes: Chwa II Kabalega (also Kabarega, Kabaleega; 1853–1923) became Omukama of Bunyoro-Kitara during the 1869–1870 succession contest and consolidated rule by 1870. The Hoima City government site and Bunyoro history list 1870–1899, while a scholarly reference treats ruling authority to 1898; historical transition in 1898 and Kabalega's military capture/exile in 1899 must not be conflated. Kabalega reformed Bunyoro's military organisation, reduced chiefly autonomy and opposed British colonial conquest. The recorded 1870–1899 interval has approximate year certainty at both boundaries and does not assert uninterrupted control over all claimed territories. The Kingdom of Bunyoro-Kitara is an independent historic polity, not a new state created specifically 'under Kabalega'.
